title: Tier watermark router: credit-led soft-demotion and regional spillback
creator: Leah Kim
body:
Summary: Design and implement a watermark-based admission and soft-demotion policy for tiered routing (free / paid / enterprise). The goal is to reduce hard rejections for free-tier bursts while preserving enterprise SLOs and predictable costs. The router will use tenant-level and plan-level watermarks (green/yellow/red) derived from credit balances and recent consumption patterns to decide admission, probability-based acceptance, and automatic demotion to cheaper fallback model variants or regional spillback.

Motivation: Existing tier routing reacts abruptly when plan credits drop below hard thresholds, causing customer-visible failures and noisy promotions/demotions during bursts. A watermark approach provides hysteresis and probabilistic smoothing to: 1) protect enterprise capacity, 2) avoid cascading fallback storms, 3) improve utilization by opportunistic acceptance when headroom exists, and 4) provide predictable degradation paths (soft demotion) before complete rejection.

Scope: This ticket covers router policy, admission control behavior, telemetry hooks, feature flags, and a canary rollout plan for US and EU regions. Implementation will touch admission controller, credit subsystem read path, routing policy config, and Console rollout UI. Fallback model variants are limited to quantized / cheaper model sizes we already support (e.g., small-quant-1, small-int8-1).

Design (high level):
- Watermarks: compute for each tenant and plan a 3-state watermark: GREEN (>= 30% credit headroom), YELLOW (10% - 30%), RED (< 10%). Thresholds configurable per plan class.
- Admission decision matrix:
  - GREEN: normal routing, best-effort batching.
  - YELLOW: probabilistic acceptance for free/paid with per-minute burst budget; enterprise remains high priority. Acceptance probability p = linear_map(headroom, 10%, 30%) for free/paid; enterprise p capped at > 0.95.
  - RED: soft-demote: route to fallback model variant if available (and matches capability), else apply stricter probability (p_min = 0.05) or queue with TTL = 200ms.
- Hysteresis: only change watermark state after a moving-average window (default 15s) to avoid flip-flop.
- Regional spillback: when local region capacity is constrained and tenant watermark is YELLOW/RED, route to alternate region with policy respecting data residency flags. For tenants with residency_lock=true, spillback is disallowed and stricter local demotion applies.
- Lease tokens: when admission grants a slot based on probabilistic acceptance, return a short-lived lease token (2000ms) to the client pipeline for KV cache and batching consistency.

Algorithm (pseudocode):
- inputs: tenant_id, plan_class, credits_remaining, recent_rate(tokens/sec), region_availability, residency_lock
- compute headroom = credits_remaining / expected_hourly_spend(tenant_id)
- watermark = moving_average_state(headroom, window=15s, thresholds=[0.3,0.1])
- if region_availability.low and plan_class != enterprise: consider spillback to compatible_region unless residency_lock
- switch watermark:
  - GREEN -> accept with p=1.0, route to preferred model
  - YELLOW -> p = clamp((headroom-0.1)/0.2, 0.05, 0.95), if random() <= p accept else try fallback model variant with same p_fallback or queue short TTL
  - RED -> if fallback_variant_available route to fallback; else p = 0.05 accept + log allocation_denied_metric; return graceful_degrade header

Config surface:
- plan-level thresholds (green/yellow/red), burst_budget_per_minute, hysteresis_window_seconds, fallback_model_priority_list, residency_override list, acceptance_seed (for deterministic testing).

Telemetry & metrics: emit tenant.watermark_state, tenant.accept_rate, tenant.fallback_rate, tenant.denial_rate, admission.latency, spillback.count, spillback.latency, fallback.model_usage. Add tags: plan_class, region, decision_path. Wire metrics to Console rollouts and cost dashboards.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flagged rollout v1 to 5% of internal traffic (dev tenants) in US region.
2) Observe metrics for 48h: denial_rate, enterprise_p99 latency, fallback_ratio.
3) Expand to 25% US and 5% EU after validation.
4) Full rollout with per-tenant opt-out.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Probability-based acceptance complexity vs deterministic token-bucket. We opted for probability because it smooths acceptance without complex leases.
- Fallback model compatibility: some requests require full-size models; fallback list must be filtered by capability.
- Cost accounting for spillback across region (cross-region egress) — requires billing coordination.

Artifacts: PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/SMART-ROUTING-WATERMARK (internal)
Design diagram: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/smart-routing/watermark-design.png
Implementation repo TODO: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/tree/feature/watermark-router

QA notes: Add deterministic tests for probabilistic gate using acceptance_seed; add chaos test that simulates credit drain and verifies hysteresis prevents flip-flop.

Acceptable failure modes: short bursts that exceed yellow acceptance result in graceful demotion to fallback model rather than immediate 403s for free tier. Enterprise customers must not observe >5% increase in p99 latency during experimentation windows.
acceptance_criteria: Router calculates tenant watermarks and exposes watermark state metric within 10s of change
Admission decisions follow probability curves for YELLOW state and are deterministic under acceptance_seed
Fallback model routing occurs for RED state when compatible variant exists and is reflected in fallback.model_usage metrics
Hysteresis prevents watermark flips for sustained oscillation test (15s window default)
Canary rollout completes with no more than 2% increase in enterprise p99 latency and denial_rate < 0.5% over 48h
